basic_info.title: NetTraj: A Network-based Vehicle Trajectory Prediction Model with Directional Representation and Spatiotemporal Attention Mechanisms
basic_info.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, 2022 (early access 2021); preprint arXiv:2106.11175 (2021)

gap_analysis.whats_missing: NetTraj represents each trajectory as a sequence of intersections plus movement directions and feeds them to an LSTM encoder-decoder, with a local graph attention mechanism for network-level spatial dependencies and a temporal attention mechanism (sliding context window) for short/long-term temporal dependencies. It uses no transformer encoder over a vectorized graph, no RL / latent-space sequential decisions, no semantic (RDF/POI) enrichment, and is trained supervised.
gap_analysis.reasoning: It captures road-network structure for trajectory prediction via LSTM + graph/temporal attention, but none of the three hybrid pillars (transformer semantic encoder, latent-space RL, label-free training) are present, so it is a structural baseline rather than an overlap.

relevance.bmw_relevance: A strong network-aware baseline for predicting where fleet vehicles travel at city scale; useful as a comparison point and for its directional / graph-attention representation of road-network trajectories in BMW Foresight.
